Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: a portable procStat for darwin using sysctl kern.proc. The changeset adds a Darwin procStat implementation that reads process data through sysctl, moves Linux parsing into its own file, and adds explicit errors for other platforms. The title refers to `#7063`, while the PR objectives cite `#8008` for the same title; the number does not affect whether the title matches the changes.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#7063` is the only active direct link. Its requirement: handoff start-time identity must work on aarch64-darwin through a portable source, or return an explicit unsupported-platform error. No bare /proc failure may remain. The reviewed head meets this. (1) procstat_darwin.go implements procStat with unix.SysctlKinfoProc("kern.proc.pid", pid). Start time is P_starttime in microseconds. Zombie is P_stat == 5 (SZOMB). This matches the portable source named in the issue (sysctl kern.proc). (2) procstat_other.go (build tag !linux && !darwin) returns an explicit 'process start time unavailable on <GOOS>' error. (3) procstat_linux.go holds the moved /proc/<pid>/stat reader. handoff.go no longer contains the /proc parser. ProcessStartTime and childAlive call the per-platform procStat, and the StartTime documentation states the units are platform-defined. (4) TestProcStatSelf adds a self-check against the kernel record. The PR description names the cross-repo follow-up (advance the mcpx pin in dezren39/nix so dezren39/nix#471 can resume), which satisfies the third criterion. Limits of this assessment: I did not run the Linux test suites or darwin-compile-check.sh. Their PASS results are author-reported. I did not verify the x/sys/unix module dependency in go.mod. I did not read procstat_test.go or procstat_linux.go directly.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** Every changed area maps to `#7063`. The changes are: removal of the Linux-only /proc parser from handoff.go (with its now-unused bytes, strconv, and strings imports); the new per-platform procstat_linux.go, procstat_darwin.go, and procstat_other.go; the TestProcStatSelf test; and documentation changes to ProcessStartTime and StdioHandoff.StartTime. The test and the documentation support the objective directly. The PR does not change the darwin takeover/upgrade support-or-refuse decision on `#237`. It does not change other /proc uses in test helpers covered by PR `#3288`. The summary lists no unrelated files. Checks used: the whole-PR file reads of the three procstat files and handoff.go at head. Not inspected: the full diff and procstat_test.go body. Those were not needed for this verdict.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 100.00% which is sufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 3 functions across 5 files.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
